anchors.quote: Conditionally formulate each pivot selection as a finite search over row indices i in [col,n). Mark exactly the first index whose absolute pivot entry is maximal: abs(rows[i][col]) is at least every remaining candidate magnitude, and no earlier remaining index has the same magnitude. This produces the same unique index as Python max with its first-index tie rule.

binding.rationale: Explicit reviewer transcription; no automatic prose-equivalence proof.

interpretations.meaning: Execute the explicitly transcribed expression on absolute pivot values.
interpretations.expression: all(values[i] >= values[k] for k in indices) and not any(values[j] == values[i] for j in indices if j < i)

interpretations.meaning: Execute the explicitly transcribed expression on absolute pivot values.
interpretations.expression: all(values[i] >= values[k] for k in indices if k != i) and not any(values[j] == values[i] for j in indices if j < i)
